newsitem.title: FRANCE: French business leaders see no rise in activity.
newsitem.headline: French business leaders see no rise in activity.

text.p: French business leaders see no significant rise in activity in the coming months, according to a monthly survey by the Bank of France.

"No sizeable upturn in activity is expected in the coming months. There should be some progress in the capital goods and food processing sectors while a significant downturn is forecast in the automobile sector," the Bank said in a statement.
Capacity utilisation rate increased slightly in September.
The Bank said that with the exception of a few products, notably petroleum and wood pulp, commodity prices were on a downward trend.
Finished goods prices remained broadly stable despite intense competition. Further falls were recorded in the car sector and in various branches of the intermediate goods sector.
Investment spending remained limited and was mainly concentrated in large firms. It was focused mostly on improving productivity.
Retail sales, which had posted a large increase in August, slipped in September, despite exceptional strength in car sales.

Unadjusted figures showed that activity in the construction sector stabilised in the third quarter compared with the previous quarter, but remained below the level recorded in the corresponding period of 1995.

Employment levels were hardly changed in the manufacturing industry, with the exception of the car and consumer goods sector, which edged down. They decreased in the building sector but remained unchanged in trade and market services.

Many fixed-term contracts were not renewed at the end of the summer, the Bank said. There was increased use of shorter time workers and a rise in planned redundancies. Some firms make widespread use of temporary labour in a bid to increase flexibility.

Order books were below normal levels in all sectors and thinned in all sectors with the exception of intermediate goods, where they nevertheless remained insufficient. Inventories were still deemed to be larger than normal, except in the car sector, where they are now below the desired level.
